title: Laser treatment may help children recover faster after dental anaesthesia
html:
Dental Tribune International

Thu. 19. November 2026

share save

BHIMAVARAM, India: The limitations of existing approaches to reversing oral numbness or preventing associated soft-tissue injuries in children after dental local anaesthesia have prompted interest in minimally invasive alternatives. Building on earlier findings in younger children, researchers in India have conducted a randomised split-mouth clinical trial to assess the effect of low-level laser therapy on recovery from oral numbness in an older age group. Their findings add to evidence that photo-biomodulation can reduce the period of numbness during which children are vulnerable to accidental soft-tissue injury such as lip or cheek biting.

The study involved 34 children aged 8–12 years undergoing bilateral primary tooth extractions under infiltration anaesthesia. Each child received photo-biomodulation on one side and sham treatment on the other during separate appointments.

Photo-biomodulation was delivered using an 810 nm diode laser in continuous mode at six predefined intra-oral and extra-oral sites. An independent examiner assessed sensation every 5 minutes, comparing the children’s responses to palpation on the anaesthetised tissue with the unaffected side.

The results showed a statistically significant difference. Mean recovery time was 17.5 minutes shorter with photo-biomodulation. The effect was observed in both jaws. The proposed explanation is that photo-biomodulation may increase local blood flow, potentially facilitating removal of residual anaesthetic.

The findings are consistent with those of a recent randomised split-mouth trial in younger children, which additionally reported a lower incidence of self-inflicted soft-tissue trauma after laser treatment. However, the present study did not assess whether the quicker return of sensation reduced self-inflicted soft-tissue injuries or difficulties with eating or speaking. Whether the shorter period of numbness translated into meaningful clinical benefits for the children in this study was thus unclear.

The article, titled “Effect of photobiomodulation on recovery from oral soft tissue local anaesthesia in paediatric patients: A preliminary split-mouth randomized clinical trial”, was published online on 28 October 2026 in Lasers in Medical Science.
